errorCodes.meaning: No namespace bound to this VTC has this identifier, or contains this resource.

DriftItem.description: One difference between the forge's observed state and the VTC's projection of a repository.

account.description: Whose role differs, for the three role types.

expected.description: What the projection calls for, in the forge's own vocabulary. Absent when the projection calls for nothing.

observed.description: What the forge shows, in the forge's own vocabulary (a role name such as `maintain`, a setting name). Absent when nothing is there.

type.description: `roleAdded` — someone holds a forge role the projection does not give them. `roleRemoved` — a projected role is missing. `roleChanged` — a projected role is present at another level. `requiredCheckMissing` — the verify-trust check is no longer required. `protectionWeakened` — branch protection or a ruleset is weaker than the projection in another way (force-push allowed, bypass actors added). `bootstrapMissing` — a bootstrap file or variable is gone.

DriftItem.title: DriftItem

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

ForgeAccount.description: A person's account on one forge. `id` is authoritative; `login` is for display only, because logins can be renamed and re-registered.

login.description: The account's current login, as the forge reported it when last seen. Display only.

ForgeAccount.title: ForgeAccount

ForgeEvent.description: One forge-neutral event, discriminated by `type`. The specification's event table says what each type means and what the VTC does with it.

role.description: The role the account now holds. Absent: the account holds no role now.

requiredCheck.description: Whether the forge still refuses merges without a passing verify-trust check, with no bypass.

ownerId.description: The forge's id for the owner, which survives renames.

ladder.description: The levels the forge offers as a direct role on a repository in the namespace, lowest first, without `none` (which every forge has). Every role in `roleMap` and in each `repos[].roleMap` is `none` or one of these.

repos.description: Repositories whose own map differs from `roleMap`, each at most once. Absent or empty: every repository uses `roleMap`.

stale.description: Repositories whose forge roles the bridge last projected under a different map from the one it now applies to them. Absent or empty: none.

action.description: `opened` — the pull request was just opened. `reopened` — a closed, unmerged pull request was reopened.
action.title: PullRequestAction

actor.description: The account that performed this action: the author for `opened`, whoever reopened the pull request for `reopened`.

author.description: The account that opened the pull request.

draft.description: Whether the pull request is a draft. Absent: the bridge does not know, or the forge has no drafts.

forgeId.description: The forge's id for the repository the pull request targets.

fromFork.description: Whether the pull request's head branch lives in another repository (a fork). Absent: the bridge does not know.

resource.description: The repository the pull request targets (its base repository).

ForgeEvent.title: ForgeEvent

ForgeHost.description: The lowercased DNS host of a forge: `github.com`, a GitHub Enterprise Server host, `codeberg.org`, `gitlab.com`, or a self-hosted Forgejo or GitLab instance such as `git.example.org`. No scheme, no port, no path. The host is a segment of every resource, so a right never crosses forges.
ForgeHost.title: ForgeHost

ForgeId.description: An identifier the forge itself assigns — a repository id, a user or organisation id — carried as a string so a forge whose ids are not numbers needs no new version. GitHub, Forgejo and GitLab ids are decimal integers written as strings (`"812736451"`). Unlike a name, it survives renames and transfers, which is why rights and bindings are keyed by it.
ForgeId.title: ForgeId

ForgeRole.description: A role in the forge's own vocabulary (`maintain`, `write`).

JobId.description: The VTC's identifier for a job, unique across the VTC's jobs.

MappedRole.description: A level of the bridge's forge-neutral role ladder, lowest first: the vocabulary role drift's `observed` and `expected` are reported in. `none` is no direct role on the repository.
MappedRole.title: MappedRole

NamespaceId.description: The VTC's opaque identifier for a namespace, assigned when it is bound. Stable for the life of the binding; never reused for another binding.
NamespaceId.title: NamespaceId

RepoResource.description: A forge-qualified resource naming exactly one repository: `<forge-host>/<owner>/<repo-path>`, lowercase, where the repository path has 1 to 21 segments (see `Resource`).
RepoResource.title: RepoResource

Response.description: The VTC has recorded the event. Nothing else is returned.
Response.title: Git Namespaces — Bridge Event — response payload

RoleMap.description: The forge role each repository right is given, as the forge applies it: after the forge's own ladder has rounded it down. `own` is the role `git.repo.own` projects to, `maintain` that of `git.repo.maintain`, `commit` that of `git.commit.sign` (`none` is fork-based contribution). There is no member for `git.ns.admin` or `git.repo.create`, which project to no forge role whatever a bridge is configured with. Ordered: `own` is at least `maintain`, which is at least `commit`, and `commit` is at most `write`.
RoleMap.title: RoleMap

schema.description: The bridge tells the VTC something happened on the forge — translated from the forge's webhook or found by an inspection sweep — together with any drift it now sees; or reports the role map it projects with, or a pull request opened or reopened on a governed repository.

drift.description: The complete outstanding drift for each repository the event concerns, replacing what the VTC held for those repositories. Absent: the event changes no repository's drift.

namespace.description: The namespace the event happened in.

schema.title: Git Namespaces — Bridge Event — payload
